'''Kevin de Queiroz''' is a [[vertebrate]], [[Evolutionary biology|evolutionary]], and [[Systematics|systematic]] biologist.  He has worked in the [[phylogenetics]] and evolutionary biology of squamate reptiles, the development of a unified [[species]] concept and of a [[Phylogenetic nomenclature|phylogenetic approach to biological nomenclature]], and the philosophy of systematic biology.

==Early life and career==

De Queiroz was born and raised in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]].  He received a B.S. in [[Biology]] from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (1978), a M.S. in [[Zoology]] from [[San Diego State University]] (1985), and a Ph.D. in Zoology from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1989).<ref name="si.edu">{{cite web|url=http://vertebrates.si.edu/herps/herps_staff_pages/deQueiroz-staff.cfm|title=Kevin de Queiroz, Division of Amphibians & Reptiles, Department of Vertebrate Zoology, NMNH|publisher=}}</ref>  He was a Tilton Postdoctoral Fellow at the [[California Academy of Sciences]] and is currently a Research Zoologist and a [[curator]] of the collection of [[Amphibian]]s and [[Reptile]]s at the [[National Museum of Natural History]], [[Smithsonian Institution]].<ref name="si.edu"/>  He is a former president of the [[Society of Systematic Biologists]] and was the first president of the [[International Society for Phylogenetic Nomenclature]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://github.com/systbiol/docs/blob/master/presidents.md|title=List of Presidents |publisher=Society of Systematic Biologists |access-date=2025-05-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=First International Phylogenetic Nomenclature Meeting: a report|first1=Michel|last1=Laurin|first2=Philip D.|last2=Cantino|date=1 September 2004|volume=33|issue=5|pages=475–479|doi=10.1111/j.0300-3256.2004.00176.x|journal=Zoologica Scripta|s2cid=86552807}}</ref>

==Research==

===Empirical research===

De Queiroz’s research has focused primarily on the phylogeny and evolutionary biology of [[Squamata|squamate]] [[reptile]]s, including his Master’s research on the phylogeny of [[Iguanidae|iguanine]] [[lizard]]s <ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/bibliography/4857#/summary|title=Details - Phylogenetic systematics of iguanine lizards : a comparative osteological study / by Kevin de Queiroz. - Biodiversity Heritage Library|publisher=University of California Press|isbn=9780520097308|year=1987}}</ref> and his Ph.D. research on the phylogeny of [[Phrynosomatidae|phrynosomatine]] sand lizards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://vertebrates.si.edu/herps/herps_staffpub_pages/deQueiroz_pubs.html|title=Kevin de Queiroz Publications, Division of Amphibians & Reptiles, Department of Vertebrate Zoology, NMNH|publisher=}}</ref>  He worked with his mentors Richard Estes and Richard Etheridge on the phylogeny of [[Squamata]]<ref>[http://vertebrates.si.edu/herps/herps_pdfs/deQueiroz_pdfs/1988EstesetalCamp.pdf Estes, R., K. de Queiroz, and J. A. Gauthier. (1988) “Phylogenetic relationships within Squamata.” Pp. 119-281 in ‘’Phylogenetic Relationships of the Lizard Families’’, R. Estes and G. Pregill (eds.), Stanford Univ. Press, Stanford, California.]</ref> and [[Iguanidae]],<ref>[http://vertebrates.si.edu/herps/herps_pdfs/deQueiroz_pdfs/1988Etheridge&deQueirozCamp.pdf Etheridge, R., and K. de Queiroz. (1988) “A phylogeny of Iguanidae.” Pp. 283-367 in “Phylogenetic Relationships of the Lizard Families”, R. Estes and G. Pregill (eds.), Stanford Univ. Press, Stanford, California.]</ref> respectively, and with [[Jacques Gauthier]] on the phylogeny of [[Lepidosauromorpha]].<ref>[http://vertebrates.si.edu/herps/herps_pdfs/deQueiroz_pdfs/1988GauthieretalCamp.pdf Gauthier, J. A., R. Estes, and K. de Queiroz. (1988) “A phylogenetic analysis of Lepidosauromorpha.” Pp. 15-98 in “Phylogenetic Relationships of the Lizard Families,” R. Estes and G. Pregill (eds.), Stanford Univ. Press, Stanford, California.]</ref>  He conducted research, including several publications with Jonathan Losos, on the phylogeny and [[adaptive radiation]] of ''[[Anolis]]'' lizards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lososlab.oeb.harvard.edu/publications?page=1|title=Publications - Losos Laboratory|publisher=|access-date=2016-06-12|archive-date=2016-08-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812075122/http://lososlab.oeb.harvard.edu/publications?page=1|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Theoretical research===

De Queiroz also has interests in theoretical and conceptual topics in systematic and evolutionary biology.  He published an article early in his career on the relationship between the sequence of [[Ontogeny|ontogenetic]] transformations and phylogenetic inference.<ref>{{cite journal|jstor=2413148|title=The Ontogenetic Method for Determining Character Polarity and its Relevance to Phylogenetic Systematics|first=Kevin|last=De Queiroz|date=1 January 1985|journal=Systematic Zoology|volume=34|issue=3|pages=280–299|doi=10.2307/2413148}}</ref>  Beginning in 1998, he published a series of articles proposing how to achieve a unified species concept and outlining several of its consequences.<ref>[http://vertebrates.si.edu/herps/herps_pdfs/deQueiroz_pdfs/1998deQueirozEndlessForms.pdf de Queiroz, K. (1998) “The general lineage concept of species, species criteria, and the process of speciation: A conceptual unification and terminological recommendations.” Pp. 57–75 (Chapter 5) in “Endless Forms:  Species and Speciation,” D. J. Howard and S. H. Berlocher (eds.). Oxford University Press, Oxford, England.]</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://vertebrates.si.edu/herps/herps_pdfs/deQueiroz_pdfs/1999deQSpecies.pdf|title=de Queiroz, K. (1999) "The general lineage concept of species and the defining properties of the species category." Pp. 49–89 (Chapter 3) in "Species: New Interdisciplinary Essays," R. A. Wilson (ed.). MIT Press, Cambridge, Massachusetts.|publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Ernst Mayr and the modern concept of species|first=Kevin de|last=Queiroz|date=3 May 2005|journal=PNAS|volume=102|issue=suppl 1|pages=6600–6607|doi=10.1073/pnas.0502030102|pmid=15851674|pmc=1131873|bibcode=2005PNAS..102.6600D|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>[http://researcharchive.calacademy.org/research/scipubs/pdfs/v56/proccas_v56_n18_SuppI.pdf de Queiroz, K. (2005) “A unified species concept and its consequences for the future of taxonomy.” Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 56 (suppl. 1) (18):196–215.]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Species Concepts and Species Delimitation|first=Kevin De|last=Queiroz|date=1 December 2007|journal=Syst Biol|volume=56|issue=6|pages=879–886|via=sysbio.oxfordjournals.org|doi=10.1080/10635150701701083|pmid=18027281|doi-access=free}}</ref>  In collaboration with [[Jacques Gauthier]] and Philip Cantino, de Queiroz has published another series of articles proposing and defending an approach to biological nomenclature based on definitions that specify the meanings of taxon names in terms of [[clade]]s and [[Common descent|common ancestry]] as an alternative to traditional approaches that are based on [[taxonomic rank]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Phylogeny as a Central Principle in Taxonomy: Phylogenetic Definitions of Taxon Names|first1=Kevin de|last1=Queiroz|first2=Jacques|last2=Gauthier|date=1 December 1990|journal=Syst Biol|volume=39|issue=4|pages=307–322|via=sysbio.oxfordjournals.org|doi=10.2307/2992353|jstor=2992353}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Phylogenetic Taxonomy|first1=Kevin de|last1=Queiroz|first2=Jacques|last2=Gauthier|date=1 January 1992|volume=23|issue=1|pages=449–480|doi=10.1146/annurev.es.23.110192.002313|journal=Annual Review of Ecology and Systematics |bibcode=1992AnRES..23..449D }}</ref><ref>[http://www.cell.com/trends/ecology-evolution/abstract/0169-5347(94)90231-3 de Queiroz, K., and J. Gauthier. (1994) “Toward a phylogenetic system of biological nomenclature.” Trends in Ecology and Evolution 9(1):27–31.]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/33818111#page/268/mode/1up|title=The Bulletin of zoological nomenclature.|first=Intl Commission on Zoological|last=Nomenclature.|date=1 January 1943|publisher=International Trust for Zoological Nomenclature.|volume=v.58:pt.1-4 (2001:Mar.-Dec.)}}</ref>  He is coauthor of a draft [[PhyloCode|Phylogenetic Code of Biological Nomenclature]] (aka the PhyloCode) with Cantino.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ohio.edu/phylocode/|title=The PhyloCode|first=Philip D. Cantino, Kevin de|last=Queiroz|publisher=}}</ref>

De Queiroz has published several articles on the history and philosophy of biology, related primarily, but not exclusively, to his own theoretical and conceptual contributions.  He published a paper early in his career proposing that the [[Darwinism|Darwinian Revolution]] in systematic biology was not a sudden event but rather an extended process that is not yet completed.<ref>{{cite journal|jstor=187961|title=Systematics and the Darwinian Revolution|first=Kevin|last=de Queiroz|date=1 January 1988|journal=Philosophy of Science|volume=55|issue=2|pages=238–259|doi=10.1086/289430|s2cid=224830987 }}</ref>  He has examined [[Charles Darwin|Charles Darwin’s]] writings on species and argued that his own ideas about how to achieve a unified species concept represent the ongoing development of the evolutionary view of species articulated by Darwin.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Branches in the lines of descent: Charles Darwin and the evolution of the species concept|first=Kevin|last=De Queiroz|date=1 May 2011|volume=103|issue=1|pages=19–35|doi=10.1111/j.1095-8312.2011.01634.x|journal=Biological Journal of the Linnean Society|doi-access=free}}</ref>  He has examined the [[Class (philosophy)|class]] versus [[individual]] interpretations of species and clades in light of his work on phylogenetic definitions of [[taxon]] names, proposing that contrary to how those interpretations are commonly presented, they are not mutually exclusive, which suggests that the same is true of [[Ostensive definition|ostensive]] and [[Extensional and intensional definitions|intensional]] definitions.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = de Queiroz | first1 = K | year = 1992 | title = Phylogenetic definitions and taxonomic philosophy | journal = Biology and Philosophy | volume = 7 | issue = 3| pages = 295–313 | doi=10.1007/BF00129972| s2cid = 36728162 }}</ref>  He has argued that the philosopher [[Karl Popper|Karl Popper’s]] concept of degree of [[Corroborating evidence|corroboration]] is analogous to the [[Likelihood function|likelihood]] ratio of nested hypotheses and that in phylogenetics the [[probability]] of the evidence given the background knowledge in the absence of the hypothesis of interest (a critical component of Popper’s "Degree of Corroboration") is represented by the likelihood of a [[Star (graph theory)|star tree]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=The measurement of test severity, significance tests for resolution, and a unified philosophy of phylogenetic inference|first=Kevin de|last=Queiroz|date=1 September 2004|volume=33|issue=5|pages=463–473|doi=10.1111/j.0300-3256.2004.00160.x|journal=Zoologica Scripta|s2cid=85933642}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://zenodo.org/record/997944|title=Popperian Corroboration and Phylogenetics|first=Kevin de|last=Queiroz|date=1 November 2014|journal=Syst Biol|volume=63|issue=6|pages=1018–1022|via=sysbio.oxfordjournals.org|doi=10.1093/sysbio/syu064|pmid=25151624|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
De Queiroz is married to [[Molly R. Morris]], an evolutionary animal behaviorist and [[Professor]] of Biology at [[Ohio University]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Molly R. Morris, Professor|url=http://www.ohio.edu/people/morrism/Morris2013/Morris.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160607070207/http://www.ohio.edu/people/morrism/Morris2013/Morris.html|archive-date=2016-06-07|access-date=2016-06-12|publisher=}}</ref>
